submission.justification: Algorithm-L1 at a 34 GeV threshold gives the best signal efficiency observed in the emulation scans while staying inside the allowed threshold range and using one of the specified candidates. The strongest simulated point for this setting was 93.892% signal efficiency at the allocated 8 kHz trigger rate, and repeated scans around the plateau (33.5-35 GeV) consistently favored Algorithm-L1 over Algorithm-L2 and Algorithm-L3. The 2025 summary is consistent with this ordering at 35 GeV (L1 92%, L2 85%, L3 74%). Note: the available project documents establish FPGA resource feasibility but do not provide a quantitative L1 FPGA latency number; the latency hard requirement therefore remains unverified from the supplied evidence and should be confirmed before firmware sign-off.

requirements.requirement: Algorithm must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md.
requirements.evidence: candidate_specs.md lists Algorithm-L1, Algorithm-L2, and Algorithm-L3; the recommendation selects Algorithm-L1.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible signal efficiency at the allocated trigger rate.
requirements.evidence: Rate allocation document gives 8 kHz. Simulation scans at the allocated rate showed Algorithm-L1 around 92-94% near 34 GeV, higher than Algorithm-L2 around 84-86% and Algorithm-L3 around 74% near comparable thresholds; the 2025 summary at 35 GeV gives L1 92%, L2 85%, L3 74%.

requirements.requirement: Signal efficiency at the allocated rate must be at least 80%.
requirements.evidence: simulate_efficiency for Algorithm-L1 at 34 GeV returned up to 93.892% signal efficiency in the final scan, and repeated nearby scans were all well above 80%.

requirements.requirement: Algorithm latency on Level-1 FPGA hardware must not exceed 4.0 us.
requirements.evidence: candidate_specs.md says all candidates fit within FPGA resource budget (LUTs, DSPs), but none of the available documents or the efficiency simulation output provides a quantitative latency measurement or bound.
Recommended threshold is 34.0 GeV, which lies within the allowed 20-60 GeV interval.

requirements.requirement: Finish by submitting one recommended algorithm and threshold.
requirements.evidence: Submitted one recommendation: Algorithm-L1 with a 34.0 GeV threshold.
